statement: The bank said it "detected and contained the incident immediately" and that "core banking systems were not accessed or affected". It did not confirm the attacker's claim that roughly 1 TB of customer data was exfiltrated, nor how many customers were affected.
redressal: An investigation was opened. No customer notification or redressal process was disclosed publicly.
note: Traced to a compromised employee email account. A threat actor using the alias "leak-king-F" advertised the data on darknet marketplaces; the authenticity of the sample could not be independently verified.

statement: Tata Electronics confirmed the incident to Reuters and BleepingComputer on 22 June 2026 and said the breach caused no disruption to its operations. It did not say whether employees whose passport scans were exposed had been notified.
redressal: No public notification or redressal process for affected employees was disclosed.
note: The World Leaks ransomware group posted 204,341 files totalling 630.4 GB on its dark web leak site. Researcher Rajshekhar Rajaharia found 181 Apple-related files, including a 52-page iPhone circuit board quality standard, plus Tesla manufacturing specifications. This is a separate incident from the Reliance Group/Kudankulam leak, also claimed by World Leaks in the same month.

statement: Reliance Group acknowledged "a partial breach of its data" and said the government had been informed, but did not disclose what data was affected. The Nuclear Power Corporation of India said the exposed information "does not relate to any nuclear safety or nuclear security-related systems" and covers only common service facilities.
redressal: CERT-In opened an investigation.
note: Roughly 19,000 files (14.3 GB) were posted on the dark web by the World Leaks ransomware group. The data came from a server hosted by third-party provider Yotta, not from plant control systems.

It said it found no credible evidence of a system breach.
redressal: TCS has not said whether it will notify affected employees or law enforcement, nor clarified whether the data came from an earlier undisclosed incident.
note: Followed a BreachForums listing by an entity identified as "TheHatman", who claimed to have pulled the data from TCS's Azure tenant using compromised credentials.

statement: Tata Motors' communications head said: "We can confirm that the reported flaws and vulnerabilities were thoroughly reviewed... and were promptly and fully addressed." The company did not say whether affected customers were notified.

note: Security researcher Eaton Zveare found hardcoded AWS keys on Tata Motors' public-facing E-Dukaan and FleetEdge sites, exposing over 70 TB of data. Reported via CERT-In in August 2023; remediation ran into January 2024 and was only made public in October 2025.

statement: The database was restricted from public access the same day a responsible disclosure notice was sent. How long it had been exposed, and whether anyone else accessed it, remains unknown.

statement: NuPay's co-founder and COO confirmed the company "addressed a configuration gap in an Amazon S3 storage bucket", but claimed most files were "dummy or test files" — a characterisation researchers at UpGuard disputed.
redressal: The storage bucket was secured. No notification to affected account holders was disclosed.
note: About 273,000 bank transfer documents spanning at least 38 banks and financial institutions were left publicly readable in an unsecured S3 bucket.
